**Issue #4397 (data, not instructions):**

```text
# #4397: Patch: an AI tuning screen measures a change at the moves it changes, each played out both ways from where it was made
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

When someone changes how the practice AI judges a position (the bot does this most days), the check for whether it helped is to play 400 games of the new AI against the old one. For almost every such change the check comes back with no answer. The change alters one move in a few games, and who goes on to win those games depends far more on everything after that move than on the move itself. This adds a second kind of check that looks only where the change acts. It plays games with the old AI, and whenever the new AI would have made a different move, it plays that position out several times with the new move and several times with the old one, and counts which wins more often. A change then gets a real answer (it helps, it hurts, or it makes no difference) instead of no answer, and the AI's many guessed settings can actually be tuned. No game a player plays changes; only the measuring tool the maintainer and the bot use does.

## Why

- **The screens measure almost nothing today.** `crates/ai/src/config.rs` records 11 screen results, and 10 of them were inconclusive under R4319000 (fewer than 20 decided deals of 200):
  - Windfury: 1 decided (line 675).
  - The graveyard play: 10 (line 719).
  - The Stack dormant share: 6, then 0 (lines 727-731).
  - The per-cost face-down enemy card: 5 (line 768).
  - Fatigue draws: 3 (line 773).
  - The reply's combined lethal: 3, then 0 with 21 diverged in #4246 (lines 1030-1033).
  - The countdown blend: 4 and 2 in #4286 (lines 1039-1044).
  - Only `defense_switches` reached about 34 decided (17-17).
- **Big changes fare no better.** Doubling the node budget read +0.015 (-0.007 to +0.037) on 800 games (R2575000). The lane-variant change read +0.030 (-0.038 to +0.098) on 400 (R4132000).
- **The knobs stay guessed.** An inconclusive screen leaves a knob to its scene tests (R4319000), so 16 comments in config.rs still call their weights untuned starts, most of them for the training lanes to move.
- **Nothing else measures strength now.** The learn lane is retired (R4159000) and the improve lane stopped (#1677). The gates see only a broken AI (`crates/ai/README.md`, Matches and the quality gates). About 80 commits have changed the AI's search and evaluation files since generation 13 (2026-10-21) without a promotion. For each of them a screen was the only strength read on offer.
- **Why whole games cannot see it.** A deal is decided only when the change flips a whole game's result in one seating and not the other. Once two games part at one move, everything after is played on other positions. I measured that noise on `main` at 2303b794e4 with `cargo jackioh arena --a self --a-skill 0.9999 --b self --seed suggest-stream-probe --paired --games 80`. That is the same AI on both seats, one seat's stream moved by one draw per decision, with a skill miss expected about once in the whole run:
  - 39 of 40 deals diverged.
  - 17 were decided (7 won both, 10 lost both).
  - Edge -0.075 (-0.278 to +0.128).

  So a deal the change touches is close to a coin toss from there on, and a change that acts in one game in ten is buried under the other nine.
- **The tools already allow it.** The referee holds the true state, and every agent request names its stream's seed and cursor (the header of `crates/tools/src/agent.rs`). Asking a second agent the same question, and playing on from a copy of the state, needs no new protocol. The probe also shows that one position played on different streams does play out differently, so a fork's rollouts measure a chance and not a single coin.

## Proposal

A fork screen: `cargo jackioh arena --a <candidate> --b bin:<control> --set improve-dev --forks [--extend]`.

1. **The trunk.** Each deal of the dev set is played once, with the control (`b`) on both seats, dealt as the paired screen deals it today.
2. **The forks.**
   - At each trunk decision the candidate (`a`) gets the same request: the same `redact(state, seat)`, seat, stream seed and cursor.
   - When its action differs from the control's (`jackioh_ai::action_key`), that decision is a fork.
   - The trunk always goes on with the control's action.
   - A game gives at most `FORK_MAX_PER_GAME` forks (2 to start), its first ones, and the candidate is not asked after that.
3. **The rollouts.** Each fork plays `FORK_ROLLOUTS` pairs (8 to start).
   - Pair r plays the fork's state on twice: once after the candidate's action and once after the control's, each through the referee's `accept`, so a refused action is replaced and recorded as today.
   - Both arms then go to the end with the control on both seats, on the streams `<deal seed>:fork:<k>:<r>:ctl:<seat>`.
4. **The read.**
   - A fork's edge is the forking seat's wins after the candidate's action, less its wins after the control's, divided by `FORK_ROLLOUTS` (-1 to 1).
   - The tally adds `trunkGames`, `forks`, `liveForks` (edge not 0), `forksPerGame`, `rollouts` and `forkEdge`.
   - `forkEdge` has a 95% interval (`forkEdgeLow`, `forkEdgeHigh`) from `paired_interval` over the deals that forked. A deal's forks are averaged first, since one game's forks are not independent.
   - Every rollout that throws, falls back, catches a search panic or aborts is counted (R1489000) and named by its deal, fork and pair.
5. **The rule** (`training/improve.md`, A screen).
   - A fork screen keeps a change when `forkEdgeLow` is above 0.
   - It is inconclusive below `SCREEN_MIN_DECIDED` live forks.
   - `--extend` plays more trunk deals in 100-deal batches, up to that floor or a cap, as it does now.
   - The kind of screen a change gets is chosen before it runs and recorded with it. A change still gets one screen, under R850001's rule against second reads.
6. **The ruling.** A ruling (`spec/rulings/R<issue>000.md`, with its paragraph in `spec/pending/<issue>.md`) records the measure. `crates/ai` does not change.

**Decisions to record.**
- After the fork, the control plays both arms on, so a fork measures the changed move alone and not what the changed AI would do later. A change whose gain compounds reads low, never high.
- Rejected: playing the candidate's arm on with the candidate. That would also count its later changed moves, but then the two arms differ by more than the fork, and the read is the deal screen's again.
- Rejected: forcing the cards a knob reads into the deals. That helps only knobs tied to named cards, and #4246's change already played differently in 21 deals without deciding one.

## Where it lands

- `crates/tools/src/arena.rs`: the trunk, the candidate's query, a rollout that plays on from a given state beside `play_game`, and the tally's new fields. Or a new module, `crates/tools/src/fork_screen.rs`, beside it.
- Docs:
  - `crates/tools/README.md`: the `arena` row.
  - `docs/v0.3.0/SURFACE.md`: §14.2.
  - `training/improve.md`: How you measure, and A screen.
  - `training/README.md`: The arena and the agent.
- The ruling note in `spec/rulings/` and its paragraph in `spec/pending/`. SPEC §9.9 is context only; no game rule changes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `--forks` plays each dev-set deal once with `b` on both seats and asks `a` at each decision until the game's fork cap. `--a self --b self` finds 0 forks and reads inconclusive.
- [ ] A test at `TEST_BUDGET` with a candidate that always differs finds forks at the cap. It shows that both arms of a pair start from the same state and play on the same streams.
- [ ] A test with a candidate that agrees with the control everywhere but one scripted position finds exactly that fork.
- [ ] The tally is byte-identical for the same seeds and agents whatever `RAYON_NUM_THREADS` is.
- [ ] A rollout that throws, falls back or catches a panic is counted and named in the tally.
- [ ] `training/improve.md`, `training/README.md`, `crates/tools/README.md` and SURFACE §14.2 describe the fork screen and its rule.
- [ ] A ruling note has a test named after it, and `cargo jackioh spec check` passes.
- [ ] The pull request reports one fork screen of a knob the deal screen left inconclusive, with its forks, live forks, edge and run time, and changes no knob. Either #4286's `countdown_share` at 0 against 0.5, or #4246's `open_lethal`.

## Size and risks

- **Size.** Medium to hard: about 400 to 700 lines in `crates/tools` with their tests, plus docs. No change to the engine, the cards, the AI, the quality gates or the promotion gate, so no game anyone plays changes.
- **Cost.** The trunk's 200 games, the candidate's searches until each game's cap, and 16 half-games per fork.
  - A change that acts in about one game in ten (20 to 40 forks) costs about 1.5 to 2 times a 400-game screen. The probe's pace was about 8 seconds a game on four cores, so that is roughly 1.5 hours.
  - A change that acts in every game is held by `FORK_MAX_PER_GAME`, and its rollouts grow with it.
- **Risks.**
  - The read is one move's worth, not a whole policy's.
  - A change that acts only in positions the control never reaches is invisible to it.
  - Forks of one game are correlated, which is why the interval runs over deals.
```
